idea.title: ConfigLint — Configuration file validator and linter for YAML/JSON/TOML

plan.tagline: CLI tool to validate and lint YAML/JSON/TOML config files with zero dependencies
plan.problem: Indie hackers and small teams waste hours debugging misconfigured YAML/JSON/TOML files that break deployments or cause silent failures
plan.solution: Run ConfigLint against any config file to get instant validation, schema checks, and linting—all via a simple CLI command with no external dependencies
plan.target_market: Solo developers, indie hackers, and small businesses managing infrastructure, apps, or automation scripts with config files
mvp_features: Validate YAML/JSON/TOML files against common schemas
Basic linting for syntax errors and style issues
Offline demo mode with hardcoded examples
SQLite-backed config history for tracking changes
plan.demo_script: Run `configlint --demo` to see 3 sample configs (YAML/JSON/TOML) validated with errors highlighted, then fix them interactively
plan.phuket_angle: Phuket-based digital nomads running small SaaS apps can use ConfigLint to validate their server configs (e.g., Docker Compose, Nginx) before deployment, avoiding downtime during peak tourist season
